settings.percentile_bound: one-sided percentile bound of the bootstrap distribution (numpy linear quantile)
settings.primitive_reading: AP3 (A415) read as AP33; literal reading as sensitivity

recommendation: Across sigma in [0, 6] the one-sided coverage (nominal 0.95) in the recall-like / concealment-like settings was: exact CP 0.905-0.964 / 0.907-0.963; dependency-graph effective-n CP 0.952-0.968 / 0.938-0.968; primitive product-weight percentile 0.959-0.979 / 0.936-0.972; first-primitive cluster percentile 0.904-0.934 / 0.878-0.926; iid bootstrap 0.879-0.948 / 0.895-0.954. Recommended cluster-robust bound: the dependency-graph effective-n CP bound (close to nominal throughout); bootstrap scheme of record: the primitive product-weight bootstrap (percentile), which is valid but conservative under weak dependence. The first-primitive cluster bootstrap under-covers and is not recommended. Percentile bounds must not be used for proportions near 1 (localisation-like setting: coverage 0.55-0.64).
scheme_decision: Connected components of the attack-primitive graph give 13 clusters, one of which holds 42 of the 58 attacks (Kish effective number of clusters 1.88); a component bootstrap would essentially resample a single unit and is reported only as a diagnostic. Test files give only 4 clusters (256 possible resamples) and are reported for completeness. The dependence is therefore handled at the primitive level, with three schemes that differ in how they treat the 25 two-primitive attacks: the product-weight bootstrap (conservative by construction: a two-primitive attack's weight has variance 3 instead of 1), the first-primitive cluster bootstrap (ignores the dependence through the second primitive) and the dependency-graph cluster-robust variance with an effective-sample-size CP bound. The calibration simulation reports their one-sided coverage under a primitive random-effects model.

worst_case_component_cp.note: perfect dependence within components; components independent

ie2_process.note_degenerate: all outcomes equal: every bootstrap distribution is a point mass at the estimate and the design effect is undefined, so the percentile bounds equal the estimate and the effective-n bounds fall back to n_eff = n (the exact CP bound); only the worst-case component bound reflects the dependence

calibration.model: y_i ~ Bernoulli(expit(b0 + sum_{p in P_i} a_p)), a_p ~ N(0, sigma^2) iid over primitives; b0 such that the design-averaged success probability equals true_mean; coverage = P(bound on the correct side of true_mean)
